problem_text:
A shipping terminal must devise a replenishment and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over an operational window spanning 18 consecutive days.  
The initial stockpile at the dawn of the planning interval is 30 barrels.  
For each day \( t = 1, \dots, 18 \), the terminal may request a delivery from its supplier; the volume of each such shipment must fall between 17 and 57 barrels.  
Every shipment, once dispatched, requires a lead time of 2 days before it becomes available for consumption or to augment the stockpile.  
The daily consumption of the additive is specified as:  
Day 1: 30 barrels  
Day 2: 47 barrels  
Day 3: 30 barrels  
Day 4: 37 barrels  
Day 5: 46 barrels  
Day 6: 59 barrels  
Day 7: 50 barrels  
Day 8: 19 barrels  
Day 9: 42 barrels  
Day 10: 37 barrels  
Day 11: 35 barrels  
Day 12: 25 barrels  
Day 13: 33 barrels  
Day 14: 34 barrels  
Day 15: 28 barrels  
Day 16: 25 barrels  
Day 17: 23 barrels  
Day 18: 26 barrels  

Deficits are tolerated; any consumption that cannot be met from on-hand stock or incoming shipments is simply lost and not carried forward.  
Throughout the 18-day horizon, additive quantities may be treated as continuous measures, and the total volume held in the terminal’s storage tanks at any moment must not surpass the capacity limit of 37 barrels.  
The aggregate expense comprises three elements: a procurement cost of 4 per barrel ordered; a storage cost of 1 per barrel kept overnight; and a penalty of 15 per barrel of unmet daily consumption.  
The objective is to decide the optimal shipment volume for each day and to monitor the ensuing stockpile and deficit levels, thereby minimizing the total expenditure.
